text:
alex_dev: Quick check — can someone confirm what TLS versions our public API and private VPC endpoints currently accept? We should be sure TLS1.0/1.1 are disabled across the board.

maria_security: Public API is on the managed LB (cloud) and enforces TLS 1.2+; we rolled 1.3 by default last quarter but kept 1.2 for some older clients. Private VPC endpoints are on internal ALBs, I think the infra team left TLS 1.2+ too.

jamal_infra: Correct — ALBs are set to TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 ciphers only. I can post the exact cipher policy: `ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS-1-2-2017-01` for 1.2 and the AWS default for 1.3.

nina_platform: For Private (on-prem/VPC) customers using our carm deployment, we rely on cert-manager issuing certs from our internal CA; certs use modern curves and support 1.3 when the client does.

alex_dev: Thanks. Two follow-ups: 1) Who owns rotation of the platform keys (controller certs, root/intermediate CA for internal cert-manager)? 2) Are any keys ever written to logs (we need to double-check redaction)?

maria_security: Ownership: root CA + intermediate rotation is owned by security (me + ops-sre for emergency), but day-to-day cert-manager certs are automated by platform (nina_platform) and stored in Vault.

jamal_infra: Agreed — certs are in Vault transit/kv depending on usage. We do not log private key material anywhere; I'll run a quick grep in the deploy logs to be safe.

rotations-bot: automated-rotation-schedule: cert-manager certs: 60d rotation, internal CA: manual review every 12 months unless compromised.

maria_security: Action item: confirm policy for customer-managed keys (BYOK) in Private — do we allow customers to upload keys to our Vault or do they bring own HSM? Nina?

nina_platform: We support two modes: 1) Customer-managed keys in their cloud KMS/HSM with grant-based access (we do not import symmetric keys), or 2) customer uploads public certs/CSRs and keeps private keys in their HSM (preferred). For Redwood-managed keys we use cloud KMS + HW-backed where available.

alex_dev: Great. One more: rotation notification & approvals — if security or infra rotates root/intermediate CA, do we have a runway to notify Dedicated/Private customers and perform coordinated rollouts?

maria_security: We have the rollout playbook in the private-deploy runbook (link: https://go.redwood/internal/runbooks/ca-rotation). Process: announce 30d, canary to internal staging, then scheduled maintenance for Dedicated customers with migration window. Private on-prem customers have to coordinate on their side — we provide signed bundle and migration script.

jamal_infra: I'll also add an automated pre-check that scans customer endpoints for TLS compatibility before any forced change.

alex_dev: Perfect. Quick policy check on logging: are we redacting any header-level secrets? e.g., Authorization bearer tokens, x-api-key, and any key material fields from uploads?

maria_security: Yes — log scrubbing filters out Authorization, x-api-key, and any field named `private_key`/`secret` before writing to structured logs. I will post the regex we use after.

rotations-bot: log-scrub-config: `regex: (?i) (authorization|x-api-key|private_key|secret) ` -> redact

jamal_infra: FYI I found one old lambda in backups that printed env variables during debug — filing a ticket to remove and rotate any exposed keys: https://tickets.redwood.com/SEC-4127

alex_dev: Thanks — can someone add a short blurb to the dedupe doc about TLS minimum version and key ownership so oncall knows where to point customers?

nina_platform: I'll add a 2-paragraph summary to the public docs and include the rotation playbook link. ETA EOD.

maria_security: I'll attach the actual regex and a short checklist for security approvals (who signs off on root rotation).

alex_dev: Awesome. For immediate closure: jamal, can you confirm by EOD that no logs contain key material? If not, create SEC ticket. Maria, please drop the regex and sign-off owner list here. Nina, add the doc blurb. I'll mark this thread resolved after updates. :thumbsup:
